$comment: Release manifest for candidate-3 (06-13-PLAN.md Task 2, 06-CONTEXT.md D-12/D-13).
Every value here is copied from a real continuous-integration run at the revision below.
Nothing in this file is measured locally. Where a lane has only local evidence, it is
recorded as BLOCKED with its reason, never as PASSED, because NOTHING LOCAL MAY BIND TO
LOCALLY BUILT BYTES (tooling/release-lanes.json).
WHAT CHANGED SINCE CANDIDATE-2, which is bound to revision 23d79e5:
* The repository-integrity workflow is GREEN. All eleven jobs succeeded, and the
all-required-passed aggregator PASSED for the first time at any candidate.
* phase2-server passes and emits a PASS line at last -- 337 cases. Its blocker was
never a leak: the Elixir compiler was quoting a deliberate hostile-input test line,
and a compatibility fixture's hard-coded support window expired mid-phase.
* phase2-sync-property and phase2-backup-restore pass; the asdf cache collision that
killed both at exit 128 before any project code ran is fixed.
* image-compose-deploy passes, having never passed at any revision. Three stacked
blockers, each visible only once the one before it was fixed.
* export-reader is wired into a required job and passes -- 16 cases.
* daily-restore passes, bound to a drill DISPATCHED AT THIS REVISION.
* 22 of 39 lanes PASS, against 14 of 39 at candidate-2 and 11 of 39 at candidate-1.
WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM, stated here so no reader has to infer it:
* daily-restore passing says NOTHING about the backup credentials it demands or about
any real object store. The credentials gate a restore that never reads them. This is
.planning/WINDOWS.md row 100 and it is not a footnote -- it is the difference between
'the restore logic works' and 'we can restore', and only the first is established.
* desktop-e2e reports 66 passing tests of which THREE passed only on retry. The three
are named in that lane's entry. Candidate-2 had no flaky line at all.
* export-elixir borrows phase2-server's suite-wide case count because it emits none of
its own. Its entry says so rather than inventing an export-only number.
* 17 lanes are BLOCKED and each says why, with an owner. Four iOS lanes, four unwired
verification lanes, three physical-blocker lanes, the trust soak, and the whole
host-replacement path.
This manifest is EXPECTED to verify non-zero. A non-zero verdict carrying stated reasons
is the honest outcome at this revision; a pass would require a release claim this
revision's evidence does not support.
Verify with:  node tooling/verify-release.mjs --manifest .planning/releases/candidate-3/release-manifest.json
Offline with: the same command plus --offline (degrades only the attestation step).
READ THE ATTESTATION LINE CAREFULLY. verify-release.mjs reports attestation=UNVERIFIED for
every artefact entry here, online and offline. That is NOT a statement that no attestation
exists -- one does, it verifies, and its decoded statement is retained under
evidence/attestation/. It is a statement that the committed entries are RECORDS of the
released bytes rather than the bytes, and the attestation is over the bytes. Closing that
gap is .planning/WINDOWS.md row 96.

THE CASE COUNT HERE IS NOT AN EXPORT-ONLY COUNT, and must not be read as one. The inventory names this lane's evidence as the phase2-server job, and that job emits ONE structured PASS line covering its whole suite: cases=337. 337 is therefore what continuous integration actually reported, and it is recorded unchanged rather than replaced by a number nobody emitted. The export suite proper is apps/server/test/keepling/application/export_test.exs, which declares 11 cases in source and is a subset of those 337. At candidate-1 and candidate-2 this lane was BLOCKED for exactly one reason -- phase2-server produced no PASS line at all -- and that reason is now gone. TO CLOSE the ambiguity rather than the lane: have the lane emit its own PASS line with its own case count, so this entry can stop borrowing the suite's.

cases=381 is the vitest case count the job reports at this revision: 306 passed across 28 files, plus 75 passed across 1 file. Identical in total to candidate-1 and candidate-2. NOTE WHAT CHANGED UNDERNEATH THAT UNCHANGED NUMBER: at revision d7e97bf, inside this phase, this lane FAILED with 305 of 306 -- `fails finitely under SQLITE_BUSY without hanging` timed out at 5000ms -- and passed at the commits either side. The test carried a comment describing the same failure once before and a fix that widened its assertion from 5s to 10s, which could never work: vitest's default testTimeout is 5000ms and the suite sets none, so the runner aborted before the widened assertion could be reached. Commit c2e4ce3, the revision this manifest is cut at, gives the test a 20s per-test timeout so its own assertion decides it. A green run at a revision where a required test was flaky is green partly by luck; this one is not.

READ THE COUNT CAREFULLY. Playwright reports `Running 66 tests`, then `3 flaky` and `63 passed (2.0m)`: 63 passed first time, 3 passed only on retry, 66 passed in total. cases=66 is the number of passing tests; it is NOT 66 clean passes, and recording 63 would understate the suite while recording 66 without this note would hide three retries. THE THREE FLAKY TESTS, named so they can be chased rather than forgotten: test/e2e/guarded-navigation.spec.ts:78 (dirty editor: Cmd-N opens the discard dialog instead of navigating), test/e2e/guarded-navigation.spec.ts:135 (keyboard-initiated Discard Changes discards and completes navigation), and test/e2e/lifecycle.spec.ts:214 (D-20: a second launch against the same profile activates the resident instance). Candidate-2 reported 66 passed with no flaky line at all, so this is a regression in stability even though the pass count is unchanged. Recorded as a new .planning/WINDOWS.md row; retry-masked flakes are exactly what QUAL-02's flake accountability exists to surface.

THIS LANE MUST BE READ WITH .planning/WINDOWS.md ROW 100, which is what makes the pass honest rather than flattering: the four KEEPLING_BACKUP_PRIMARY_* credentials the job demands GATE this drill but are never READ by it. tooling/verify-restore.sh restores packages/contracts/vectors/recovery.json, a committed fixture, into a disposable local target. The drill would pass identically with wrong credentials. What it proves is that restore and verification run end to end on a clean hosted runner, that all five corrupt fixtures are rejected, and that the epoch rotates to a semantically complete target. What it CANNOT support is any claim that a byte was fetched from object storage, that the primary bucket holds a restorable backup, or anything about real RPO.

lanes.reason: Scheduled lane (recovery-drills.yml). NOT DISPATCHED AT THIS REVISION, and that is the only thing wrong with it. The fixture itself passes: it was dispatched two commits earlier at revision af49e08 as run 34777715708 and succeeded, the first time this drill has ever passed, on the same credential provisioning that unblocked daily-restore. But run 34778845662 at c2e4ce37ff0ca2c27067b098c2cfbdc59155ba96 selected drill=newest-logical, which runs both daily fixtures and SKIPS this job, so no evidence exists at the revision this manifest is cut at. A pass at a nearby revision is not a pass at this one, and is not recorded as one. TO CLOSE, one command: `gh workflow run recovery-drills.yml --ref main -f drill=historical-pitr` at this revision, then bind its evidence here. Row 100's caveat applies to it exactly as it applies to daily-restore.

Two independent things block this lane, and provisioning the credentials fixed neither. FIRST, the job body hardcodes `result: NON_PASSING` and `exit 1` before it reads any token, so it cannot pass whatever secrets exist; it has no runtime provisioning and materialises none of the five credential FILES the lane needs. SECOND, tooling/verify-host-replacement.sh requires eight inputs, five of them files outside the repository, and two of those inputs are not yet decided at all -- the DNS record name for the app host, and an SSH public key item. HCLOUD_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN are now provisioned in the recovery-live environment (which had to be created; it did not exist), so the credential half is genuinely started, but the workflow half is untouched. DATA-03 and OPS-02 stay unchecked, which is the honest outcome. See .planning/WINDOWS.md row 95 as amended.

Protected outer lane. CHANGED AT THIS REVISION, and the change is real but does not make it passable. Commit 1195bdc replaced the hardcoded deferral in tooling/test-phase-2.sh with a check of all nine required inputs: with every input present the lane now actually invokes tooling/verify-host-replacement.sh, and with any input absent it defers and NAMES the absent ones. Tested at eight of nine inputs, it still defers. So the lane is no longer structurally incapable of running -- but it still has no committed job that supplies those inputs (see quarterly-host-replacement above), so it has not run, and it reports BLOCKED with a zero case count. It provisions a real paid host and real DNS and is single-attempt; it keeps exiting non-zero so that no skip is ever counted as evidence.
